skills.name: Modus Ponens
skills.description: Affirming the antecedent: if P implies Q and P holds, then Q follows. Covers both propositional and first-order logic forms, and addresses the common failure of hedged conditionals.

skills.name: Modus Tollens
skills.description: Denying the consequent: if P implies Q and Q is false, then P is false. Covers propositional and first-order logic. Addresses the hardest failure modes: narrative-context confusion and treating the conclusion as uncertain.

skills.name: Disjunctive Syllogism
skills.description: Eliminating a disjunct: if P or Q (inclusive), and not P, then Q. Covers propositional and first-order logic. Addresses inclusive vs. exclusive OR confusion and scope issues.

skills.name: Hypothetical Syllogism
skills.description: Chaining conditionals: if P implies Q and Q implies R, then P implies R. Covers propositional and first-order logic. Addresses premature chain-breaking and denying-the-antecedent errors.

skills.name: Constructive Dilemma
skills.description: Derives a disjunction of consequents (Q∨S) from two conditionals (P→Q, R→S) and a disjunction of antecedents (P∨R).

skills.name: Destructive Dilemma
skills.description: Derives a disjunction of negated antecedents (¬P∨¬R) from two conditionals (P→Q, R→S) and a disjunction of negated consequents (¬Q∨¬S).

skills.name: Bidirectional Dilemma
skills.description: Derives Q∨¬R from two conditionals (P→Q, R→S) and a mixed disjunctive premise (P∨¬S) combining one antecedent with one negated consequent.

skills.name: Commutativity of Disjunction
skills.description: Reasoning about the logical equivalence P∨Q ≡ Q∨P, distinguishing genuine commuted forms from disjunctions that involve negated propositions.

skills.name: Material Implication
skills.description: Reasoning with the equivalence P→Q ≡ ¬P∨Q, identifying which disjunctive forms are and are not logical consequences of a given conditional.

skills.name: Existential Generalization
skills.description: Reasoning from a named individual with a property to the existence of at least one such individual, without over-generalizing to universal claims.

skills.name: Universal Instantiation
skills.description: Applying a universally quantified statement to a named individual, reasoning strictly from premises without overriding them with real-world knowledge.

skills.name: Reasoning About Explicit Exceptions
skills.description: Reasoning about disjunctive exceptions to default rules: when 'either A or B' fails to have property P, tracking what follows for the exception members and for non-named entities in the group.

skills.name: Reasoning About Named Individual Exceptions
skills.description: Reasoning about named single-entity exceptions to population-level defaults: determining what can be concluded about the wider group and the precise count of exceptions when a specific individual violates the norm.

skills.name: Reasoning About Chained Default-Exception Structures
skills.description: Reasoning about exceptions in multi-level default chains: tracking which level an exception applies to, determining whether it propagates to specific subcategory members, and preserving intact defaults for non-implicated entities.

skills.name: Reasoning Under Conflicting Evidence: Priority and Reliability
skills.description: Non-monotonic reasoning under priority: when two sources make contradictory claims, the more reliable source's assertion is adopted as the conclusion — a defeasible rule, not merely a probabilistic weight.

skills.name: Default Reasoning with a Single Exception
skills.description: Applying a default rule to a non-exceptional member when one member of the class is explicitly designated as the exception.

skills.name: Default Reasoning with Irrelevant Information
skills.description: Applying a default rule correctly by filtering out logically irrelevant premises that do not affect who the exception is or the scope of the default.

skills.name: Default Reasoning under an Open-World Assumption
skills.description: Reasoning that a default holds for all members of a category except the explicitly named exception, without appealing to real-world knowledge that goes beyond the given context.

skills.name: Default Reasoning with Multiple Concurrent Defaults
skills.description: Applying two concurrent default rules when each of two individuals is the exception to a different default, yielding cross-default conclusions about which individual satisfies which property.
